# Configuration

The server reads `wpg.toml` from the working directory, or the file given with `--config` / `WPG_CONFIG`. Precedence, lowest first: built-in defaults, the file, environment variables `WPG_<SECTION>__<KEY>` (`__` separates nesting levels, for example `WPG_SERVER__BIND=0.0.0.0:8080` or `WPG_TX__ALLOWED_IFACES='["eth1"]'`), then command line options such as `wpg serve --bind`. Unknown keys are errors. `wpg config init` writes the commented example below, `wpg config show` prints the effective configuration, `wpg config validate` checks it and `wpg config set-password` stores the admin password hash. The admin password itself is not a key: `wpg serve --password`, `--password-file` and `WPG_PASSWORD` take precedence over `auth.password_hash` and `auth.password_file`. This page is generated from the configuration types.

## Keys

### Top level

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data_dir` | `string` | OS data directory (Linux: `~/.local/share/wpg`) | `WPG_DATA_DIR` | Directory for server state: user templates, favourites, the SQLite database (users, sessions, job history), dry-run captures and the self-signed TLS certificate. |

### `[auth]`

Authentication.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `password_file` | `string` |   | `WPG_AUTH__PASSWORD_FILE` | File holding the admin password: an argon2 PHC string, or plain text that is hashed at startup. |
| `password_hash` | `string` |   | `WPG_AUTH__PASSWORD_HASH` | argon2id PHC string of the admin password; `wpg config set-password` writes it. |
| `session_ttl_secs` | `integer` | `86400` | `WPG_AUTH__SESSION_TTL_SECS` | Session lifetime in seconds (sliding: every request extends it). |

### `[log]`

Logging.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ansi` | `boolean` | `true` | `WPG_LOG__ANSI` | Colour the console output when it is a terminal. |
| `file` | `string` |   | `WPG_LOG__FILE` | Also write to this file (its directory is created). |
| `format` | `"pretty"` \| `"json"` | `"pretty"` | `WPG_LOG__FORMAT` | Line format: `pretty` (human readable) or `json` (one object per line). |
| `level` | `string` | `"info"` | `WPG_LOG__LEVEL` | Filter directives (`RUST_LOG` overrides them), for example `info` or `wpg_tx=debug,info`. |
| `max_files` | `integer` |   | `WPG_LOG__MAX_FILES` | Keep at most this many rotated files (the oldest are deleted). |
| `rotation` | `"never"` \| `"hourly"` \| `"daily"` | `"never"` | `WPG_LOG__ROTATION` | Rotation of the file: `never`, `hourly` or `daily`. |

### `[protocols]`

User-defined protocols.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dirs` | `string[]` | `[]` | `WPG_PROTOCOLS__DIRS` | Directories of user-defined protocol files (`*.yaml`: new protocol definitions and bindings under existing protocols), loaded at startup in file name order. `wpg serve --protocols-dir` adds more. |

### `[server]`

HTTP listener.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | `string` |   | `WPG_SERVER__BASE_URL` | Public URL of the server behind a reverse proxy (`https://wpg.example.net`), used for absolute links. |
| `bind` | `string` | `"127.0.0.1:8080"` | `WPG_SERVER__BIND` | Listen address. Without a password (and no user created on the setup screen) only loopback addresses are accepted (`--allow-insecure` overrides). |
| `self_signed_tls` | `boolean` | `false` | `WPG_SERVER__SELF_SIGNED_TLS` | Serve HTTPS with a self-signed certificate generated into `<data_dir>/tls/` (reused on later starts); `wpg serve --tls` sets it. |

### `[server.tls]`

TLS certificate chain and private key (PEM) to serve HTTPS with; takes precedence over `self_signed_tls`.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cert` | `string` |   | `WPG_SERVER__TLS__CERT` | PEM certificate chain. |
| `key` | `string` |   | `WPG_SERVER__TLS__KEY` | PEM private key. |

### `[templates]`

Template library.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `library_paths` | `string[]` | `["./templates"]` | `WPG_TEMPLATES__LIBRARY_PATHS` | Read-only template libraries (Git checkouts, for example), scanned recursively for `*.wpg.yaml` / `*.wpg.json` and reloaded when files change. |
| `user_dir` | `string` |   | `WPG_TEMPLATES__USER_DIR` | Writable directory for templates created or imported in the GUI; default `<data_dir>/templates`. |

### `[terminal]`

Web terminal: SSH / Telnet sessions the server opens for logged-in users (see the web terminal guide).

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed_targets` | `string[]` | `[]` | `WPG_TERMINAL__ALLOWED_TARGETS` | Targets sessions may connect to: `host`, `host:port`, `*.domain`, an IP address or a CIDR block (`10.0.0.0/8`, `[2001:db8::1]:830`); empty = any target. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `WPG_TERMINAL__ENABLED` | Enable the web terminal. Off by default. |
| `idle_timeout_secs` | `integer` | `1800` | `WPG_TERMINAL__IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS` | Close a session after this many seconds without input or output; `0` = never. |
| `max_sessions` | `integer` | `8` | `WPG_TERMINAL__MAX_SESSIONS` | Maximum number of simultaneous sessions (all users). |
| `record_sessions` | `boolean` | `true` | `WPG_TERMINAL__RECORD_SESSIONS` | Allow session logs (what the remote side sends) under `<data_dir>/terminal-logs`; `false` disables server-side logs. |

### `[tx]`

Transmit policy and defaults.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed_ifaces` | `string[]` | `[]` | `WPG_TX__ALLOWED_IFACES` | Interfaces jobs may send on; empty = all. The `null` backend and dry runs are not restricted. |
| `default_backend` | `string` |   | `WPG_TX__DEFAULT_BACKEND` | Backend used when a job names none (`null`, `pcapfile`, `afpacket`, `pcap`, `afxdp`, `dpdk`); unset = `afpacket` on Linux, else `pcap`, else `null`. |
| `dpdk_eal_args` | `string[]` | `[]` | `WPG_TX__DPDK_EAL_ARGS` | DPDK EAL arguments for the `dpdk` backend, e.g. `["-a", "0000:00:04.0"]`. wpg adds `-l <first CPU>` and `--in-memory` unless given. EAL starts once per process with the first `dpdk` job; changing them needs a restart. |
| `max_rate` | `string` |   | `WPG_TX__MAX_RATE` | Highest rate a job may request (`100kpps`, `1Gbps`); jobs without a rate are sent at this rate. |

## Example (`wpg config init`)

Every active line equals the built-in default, so the file changes nothing until edited; the commented lines show the optional keys.

```toml
# wpg.toml — Web Packet Generator configuration.
#
# Precedence (lowest first): built-in defaults < this file < environment variables
# (WPG_<SECTION>__<KEY>, e.g. WPG_SERVER__BIND=0.0.0.0:8080 or
# WPG_TX__ALLOWED_IFACES='["eth1"]') < command line options (wpg serve --bind ...).
# Unknown keys are rejected. Check a file with `wpg config validate`, print the
# effective configuration with `wpg config show`.

# Server state: user templates, favourites, job history, dry-run captures.
# Default: the OS data directory (Linux: ~/.local/share/wpg).
# data_dir = "/var/lib/wpg"

[server]
# Listen address. Without a password keep it on localhost.
bind = "127.0.0.1:8080"
# Public URL when running behind a reverse proxy.
# base_url = "https://wpg.example.net"
# Serve HTTPS with a self-signed certificate generated into <data_dir>/tls/
# (same as `wpg serve --tls`). Ignored when [server.tls] is set.
self_signed_tls = false

# TLS certificate chain and private key (PEM) to serve HTTPS with.
# [server.tls]
# cert = "/etc/wpg/cert.pem"
# key = "/etc/wpg/key.pem"

[auth]
# Admin password. Without one (and without a user created on the first-run
# setup screen) the server only listens on localhost. Sources, highest first:
# `wpg serve --password`, `--password-file`, $WPG_PASSWORD, password_hash,
# password_file, the setup screen.
# argon2id hash of the admin password (`wpg config set-password` writes it):
# password_hash = "$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$..."
# Or a file holding the hash or the plain-text password:
# password_file = "/etc/wpg/password"
# Session lifetime in seconds (extended by every request).
session_ttl_secs = 86400

[templates]
# Read-only template libraries (Git checkouts etc.), scanned recursively for
# *.wpg.yaml / *.wpg.json and reloaded when files change.
library_paths = ["./templates"]
# Writable directory for templates created or imported in the GUI.
# Default: <data_dir>/templates
# user_dir = "/var/lib/wpg/templates"

[protocols]
# Directories of user-defined protocol files (*.yaml), loaded at startup.
# Changes need a restart.
# dirs = ["/etc/wpg/protocols.d"]

[tx]
# Interfaces jobs may send on; empty = all. The null backend and dry runs are
# not restricted.
allowed_ifaces = []
# Highest rate a job may request, e.g. "100kpps" or "1Gbps". Jobs without a rate
# are sent at this rate.
# max_rate = "100kpps"
# Backend when a job names none: null, pcapfile, afpacket, pcap, afxdp, dpdk.
# Default: afpacket on Linux, else pcap, else null.
# default_backend = "afpacket"
# DPDK EAL arguments for the dpdk backend (wpg adds "-l <first CPU>" and
# "--in-memory" unless given). EAL starts with the first dpdk job; changing them
# needs a restart.
# dpdk_eal_args = ["-a", "0000:00:04.0"]

[log]
# Filter directives (RUST_LOG overrides this), e.g. "info" or "wpg_tx=debug,info".
level = "info"
# "pretty" or "json".
format = "pretty"
# Also write to this file (its directory is created).
# file = "/var/log/wpg/wpg.log"
# Rotation of the file: "never", "hourly" or "daily".
rotation = "never"
# Keep at most this many rotated files.
# max_files = 7
# Colour the console output when it is a terminal.
ansi = true

[terminal]
enabled = false          # Web terminal (SSH / Telnet)
allowed_targets = []     # "host", "host:port" or CIDR; empty = any target
record_sessions = true   # keep session logs under <data_dir>/terminal-logs
idle_timeout_secs = 1800
max_sessions = 8
```
